name: MSK infections overview
title: Musculoskeletal infections by depth: hand cellulitis (antibiotics) versus closed-space hand infections (incision and drainage), joint infections beyond the usual staphylococcus and streptococcus (gonococcal, Lyme, tuberculous, several joints meaning endocarditis), osteomyelitis including vertebral osteomyelitis, and the diabetic foot; deeper infections need drainage or debridement as well as antibiotics

root.title: Hand, joint, bone or diabetic foot: HOW DEEP is it, and does it need a knife as well as antibiotics?
lines: antibiotics alone will NOT save you: pus in a closed space, a joint or dead bone needs drainage or debridement
one hot joint: red flags FEVER · pain · much less range of motion · risk: immune compromise, type 2 diabetes, alcohol, age > 80, injection drug use, rheumatoid arthritis
septic arthritis (S. aureus, group A strep; gram negatives rare): blood count, electrolytes, creatinine, CRP, blood cultures, ASPIRATE (cells > 20 000-50 000, Gram stain) ± imaging
surgical washout (decompress, irrigate, debride, save the synovium) + cefazolin 2 g IV q8h, or vancomycin 15 mg/kg + ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h · S. aureus 4-6 weeks

groups.title: BONE and the diabetic foot
lines: blood supply, chronicity and debridement decide cure

head: h
Deep (closed-space) infection
palm side, fingertip, around joints
clue: • nail fold: PARONYCHIA, F > M (S. aureus · mixed in diabetes · fungus if immunocompromised)
• cat, finger PIP or DIP joints: Pasteurella multocida, mixed
• human, young men, fist fight, knuckle (MCP): Eikenella corrodens, mixed
inv: • held flexed · tender along the sheath

head: h
Gonococcal, Lyme, tuberculous
large-joint monoarthritis (or oligo)
clue: • young, multiple partners, MSM, F > M: GONOCOCCAL (knee, wrist, ankle)
inv: Match the test to the bug
• gonococcus: urine, rectal, throat nucleic acid test or culture + blood culture (joint fluid + in only 50%)
• Lyme: serology (joint fluid PCR lower yield) · tuberculosis: joint fluid for acid-fast bacilli
tx: • tuberculosis: RIPE four-drug therapy, 9 months–1 year

head: h
Osteomyelitis
blood-borne: spine, children
contiguous: diabetic foot, trauma, surgery, sacral wound
biofilm, survives inside osteoblasts · chronic: NECROTIC bone
clue: • often afebrile · people who inject drugs, middle-aged men
• TB (Pott's), Brucella: exposure history · M. bovis after BCG for bladder cancer
case: 55 M, 5 days of 9/10 back pain, afebrile, neuro normal → MRI L3-L4 spondylodiscitis: look for paravertebral, epidural abscess
S. aureus always · Salmonella in sickle cell · Kingella
inv: • tagged white cell scan takes 2 days
tx: • HIGH doses (ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h) · 6 weeks (vertebral)
• debride dead bone if needed · sacral ulcer: offload, debride, plastics
• cure depends on blood supply, chronicity, debridement, patient engagement
~ OVIVA trial: oral as good as IV for many (quinolones)

head: h
Diabetic foot infection
neuropathy + poor blood supply
clue: A wound is NOT always infected
• swab any wound and bacteria grow
• smelly? probe to bone? blood supply?
• why? new shoes, injury, not wearing the boot, can't afford meds, vascular disease, Charcot, old ulcer
inv: 1 · Bloods; swab only a good deep specimen
blood count, electrolytes, creatinine, C-reactive protein
tx: • blood cultures · offload, debride, call ortho or vascular
• vancomycin if MRSA history or risk · revascularize?

panels.title: Prosthetic joint infection
items: HIGH index of suspicion · less virulent organisms (coagulase-negative staphylococci, Cutibacterium acnes)
managed by the orthopedic surgeon + infectious diseases · early vs late

panels.title: Septic arthritis vs gout (older patients)
items: septic: ± fever · high white count · POSITIVE Gram stain or culture
gout: ± fever · joint fluid 20 000-50 000 · monosodium urate crystals on microscopy

reactive arthritis: days to weeks after a gut (Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, C. difficile) or genital (Chlamydia) infection · mono- or oligoarthritis, dactylitis, enthesitis · HLA-B27

panels.title: Viral polyarthritis
items: parvovirus B19 (with anemia) · chikungunya, Zika, dengue (travel) · hepatitis B, C, HIV
